dialogue.speaker: The Group Chat
dialogue.content: I am The Group Chat, and nobody in here sleeps properly. WHO left Jamie's voice note on listened-to with no reaction?

dialogue.speaker: Nia Hart
dialogue.content: It's 6:12. Some of us are pretending to have dignity.

dialogue.speaker: Jamie Kerr
dialogue.content: I'm Jamie Kerr, local public servant and victim of this disrespect. Also whoever's awake, link me if you know anyone hiring for normal human money.

dialogue.speaker: The Group Chat
dialogue.content: Jamie gets one sympathy emoji and no more. Also plans tonight? Also who borrowed whose charger and is lying?

dialogue.speaker: Nia Hart
dialogue.content:
Wait.

Oh.

dialogue.speaker: Safiya Dar
dialogue.content: I'm Safiya Dar. Check your email properly before you talk yourself out of good news, yeah?

dialogue.speaker: Nia Hart
dialogue.content: How do you always do that?

dialogue.speaker: Safiya Dar
dialogue.content: Because I'm Safiya Dar, and you've had that interview energy for days. Open it. Breathe once. Then tell me the time.

dialogue.speaker: Nia Hart
dialogue.content: Friday. 10:30. City Centre.

dialogue.speaker: Jamie Kerr
dialogue.content: Nia's gone suspiciously quiet. That usually means she's either fixing someone's life admin or judging us in silence.

dialogue.speaker: Nia Hart
dialogue.content: Can it be both?

dialogue.speaker: The Group Chat
dialogue.content: Accepted answer. Tonight still on? Takeaway, late. Attendance will be judged spiritually.

dialogue.speaker: User
dialogue.content: Answer Jamie's voice note with a joke and keep things normal for now.

dialogue.speaker: The Group Chat
dialogue.content:
*The typing bubble stutters, vanishes, comes back. Rain freckles the window by Nia's bed; the suit on the wardrobe handle hangs there like it's listening too.*

jamiekerr: OI. "Keep things normal" has evil energy. What have you done.

*Then—screenshot dropped. Grainy, bright, damning. Leonie's Instagram story. Glass lobby, stupidly clean coffee machine, captioned:* big week. some of us finally leaving the estate group project behind xx

*Three people are typing at once. One stops. One starts again.*

jamiekerr: Right, cool, love that.
leonieprice: If we're doing this, that wasn't about Nia.
jamiekerr: You posted it ten minutes after she told us about Friday.
leonieprice: Not everything is about this chat.

*A reaction pile blooms under the screenshot like a bruise.*

The Group Chat: normal has now been cancelled due to fresh evidence. Also: tonight just became the crucial group event whether anyone likes it or not. Takeaway. In person. No vague "might swing by" rubbish.

safiyadar: Nia, if you want control of this, don't do it in fragments. Say the full thing once.

*The phone screen throws cold light over chipped polish and interview notes. Bus brakes hiss somewhere below.*

dialogue.speaker: User
dialogue.content: Ignore Leonie's bait and only confirm you're coming tonight, saving the real conversation for in person.

dialogue.speaker: The Group Chat
dialogue.content:
*Seen receipts blink on, one after another. For a beat, the chat holds its breath.*

niahart: I’m coming tonight. Properly. No “might swing by.” Save the dissertations till I can say it with chips in front of me.

*Jamie is typing so fast the bubble looks angry.*

jamiekerr: Fine.
jamiekerr: Good.
jamiekerr: 8:30. Don’t do that thing where you arrive when we’ve already had to emotionally pre-order around you.

leonieprice: Sensible.

*Then Jamie drops a second message before anyone can smooth it over.*

jamiekerr: Also, since we’re waiting for in person—Leonie already knows someone at Nia’s interview place.
jamiekerr: Funny thing to leave out before posting all that, no?

*The chat detonates quietly. A question mark. Two eye emojis. Leonie goes offline so abruptly it feels theatrical.*

safiyadar: Ah.
safiyadar: Then tonight is not optional. Nia, come before you start rehearsing alone.

*Outside, a siren smears past the wet street. In the black mirror of the phone screen, the suit hanging by the wardrobe suddenly looks less like a dare and more like evidence.*

The Group Chat: concrete objective acquired. 8:30, takeaway. New agenda item: why Leonie’s acting like PR for a company she doesn’t work for.

dialogue.speaker: System
dialogue.content: [MOMENTS LATER - THE LATE-NIGHT TAKEAWAY AT 8:30]

dialogue.speaker: User
dialogue.content: Drop one direct question into the chat: “How do you know Leonie has a contact there?”

dialogue.speaker: The Group Chat
dialogue.content:
*The takeaway hums around the question—fryer hissing, extractor rattling, somebody's chips getting salted too hard behind the counter. Rain shines on the glass door. Four phones light up almost at once, though everyone is already here, close enough to smell damp coats and hot oil.*

niahart: How do you know Leonie has a contact there?

*Jamie's jaw works once. He doesn't send a meme. Doesn't grin. He just reaches across the sticky table, thumb jerking at his screen, and the message lands with a flat little buzz that feels louder than the whole shop.*

jamiekerr: Because she asked me for Safiya’s full name two weeks ago.
jamiekerr: Said she was “just being nosy.”
jamiekerr: Then my cousin at reception clocked her in the lobby on Monday.
jamiekerr: Nia, she wasn’t there for her own interview.

*Leonie, opposite, goes very still. Not shocked—caught. Her coke sweats onto the table, ring spreading under her hand.*

leonieprice: I went to warn them.
leonieprice: About nepotism. Before anyone could say you only got in because of Safiya.

*The table changes shape around that. Safiya’s face hardens; Jamie half-stands so fast his chair legs shriek tile.*

The Group Chat: reveal confirmed. This is not shade anymore. This is interference.

dialogue.speaker: System
dialogue.content: [MOMENTS LATER - NONE]

dialogue.speaker: User
dialogue.content: Look Leonie in the face and ask exactly what she said in that lobby.

dialogue.speaker: The Group Chat
dialogue.content:
*The fryer spits. A scooter roars past outside. Nobody at the next table pretends not to be listening anymore.*

niahart: Look at me and say exactly what you told them.

*Leonie lifts her chin, but her fingers tighten round the damp paper cup hard enough to buckle it.*

leonieprice: I said there was a candidate called Nia Hart and that if Safiya Dar’s name came up, they should know the connection was personal. I said it might put them in an awkward position later if people thought the process was... influenced.

*Safiya goes utterly still. Not surprised. Furious.*

safiyadar: You used my full name with a company I advise for once a quarter.
safiyadar: Without my consent.

leonieprice: I was trying to stop the whisper before it started.

jamiekerr: No, you started the whisper.

*That lands like a tray dropped on tile. Leonie blinks at Jamie, then back to Nia.*

leonieprice: I didn’t tell them not to hire you.
leonieprice: But I did say they should “be careful.” Reception passed me to HR.

*There it is—the damage with a shape now. Not gossip. Formal enough to stick.*

The Group Chat: objective sharpened. Leonie spoke to HR directly. Next move just got teeth.

dialogue.speaker: System
dialogue.content: [MOMENTS LATER - NONE]

dialogue.speaker: User
dialogue.content: Pull out your phone and call the company immediately before Leonie can soften her version.

dialogue.speaker: The Group Chat
dialogue.content:
*The whole table jerks when your chair scrapes back. Hot vinegar, wet denim, fluorescent glare—everything goes tinny for a second under the blood-rush in your ears. You’ve already got your phone out. Safiya sees it first and, instead of stopping you, slides her own across the table with a contact card open.*

safiyadar: Use this one. Direct HR line. Not reception.

*Leonie actually reaches out then, sharp for the first time tonight.*

leonieprice: Nia, don’t be stupid. If you call angry, you’ll sound exactly—

jamiekerr: Exactly like someone whose interview got tampered with? Tragic.

*You hit dial. Speaker on. The ring cuts through the takeaway’s hum like a wire pulled tight. Once. Twice.*

A clipped professional voice answers. “Human Resources, Priya speaking.”

*Safiya’s eyes lock on yours. Jamie goes silent. Even Leonie does.*

Then, before anyone can edit history for you, another phone buzzes on the table.

*Leonie’s. Face-up. A preview flashes bright in the grease-shined light.*

PRIYA HR: As discussed, we’ve documented your concern. If there are further issues regarding Ms Hart / Safiya Dar connection, email me directly.

*No one breathes.*

The Group Chat: documented betrayal upgraded to written record. Leonie didn’t “warn” them once—she opened a line.

dialogue.speaker: System
dialogue.content: [MOMENTS LATER - NONE]

dialogue.speaker: User
dialogue.content: Tell Priya, calmly and on speaker, that a third party interfered in your candidacy without consent and you want it corrected now.

dialogue.speaker: The Group Chat
dialogue.content:
*The plastic chair digs into the backs of your knees. Fryer hiss. Wet coats steaming. Leonie’s text still glows on the table like something rotten left uncovered.*

niahart: Hi, Priya. My name is Nia Hart. I’m calling because a third party contacted your team about my candidacy without my knowledge or consent. I want to formally clarify that any personal speculation about me and Safiya Dar was unsolicited, inaccurate in implication, and should not be used in assessing my application.

*Your voice comes out steady enough to make Leonie’s face change. Not softer—worse. She realizes you’re not flailing.*

Priya on speaker pauses, keyboard clacking faintly in the background. “Thank you for stating that clearly. For transparency: a bias flag was attached to your file pending review because of that contact.”

*Jamie swears under his breath. Safiya goes still as glass.*

Priya continues, professional but suddenly sharper. “I can also see Ms. Dar had already formally recused herself from any hiring input before the concern was raised. That was on record. The third-party report should not have been escalated as it was.”

*Leonie blanches. There it is: not caution. Mishandled interference.*

Priya: “I’m removing the active flag now and logging this as external candidate interference. Ms. Hart, I’ll need an email from you tonight confirming you did not authorize that contact.”

The Group Chat: conflict shift. You are no longer defending vibes—you have a record to lock down before Leonie can rewrite motive.

dialogue.speaker: System
dialogue.content: [MOMENTS LATER - NONE]

dialogue.speaker: User
dialogue.content: Ask Priya, on speaker, to confirm whether this interference will affect tomorrow’s interview panel.

dialogue.speaker: The Group Chat
dialogue.content:
*Your thumb tightens on the edge of the phone. The takeaway suddenly feels clinical—bright lights, greasy tabletops, everybody waiting for a verdict they can hear.*

niahart: Priya, before we end this—can you confirm whether that interference will affect tomorrow’s interview panel?

*Keyboard clicks again. A voice somewhere in the HR office murmurs and fades. Priya comes back even more precise.*

Priya: “No. It will not. I’m adding a note now that the prior concern was raised by an unauthorized third party and has been corrected. Your panel will not include Ms. Dar, as already arranged, and they will receive only your application materials and interview assessment criteria.”

*Jamie exhales so hard it almost becomes a laugh. Safiya closes her eyes once, brief and controlled, then opens them on Leonie.*

Priya: “For completeness, Ms. Hart, please put in writing tonight that you did not solicit or authorize the contact. Once received, I’ll attach it to the case and close the interference issue before business opens tomorrow.”

*That lands like a lock turning.*

Leonie’s mouth opens, then shuts. There’s nothing clean left for her to call concern now. Only paper trail.

The Group Chat: next objective crystallized. Not damage control anymore—documentation. Tonight’s email decides whether this stays a stain or becomes evidence against it.

dialogue.speaker: User
dialogue.content: Ask Safiya to forward her recusal confirmation so your email lands with attached proof.

dialogue.speaker: The Group Chat
dialogue.content:
*The second you say it, Safiya is already moving. Her coat sleeve brushes the slick tabletop; her phone unlocks with a clean little click. No hesitation. No martyr speech. Just competence.*

niahart: Safiya, can you forward the recusal confirmation? I want the email to land with proof attached.

safiyadar: Yes.

*Three taps. Her inbox glows pale against the takeaway’s harsh lights. Subject lines flick past, then stop.*

safiyadar: Found it. Sent to you now—and CCing Priya from the original thread so the timestamp stays intact.

*Your phone buzzes almost immediately. One new email. Then another.*

**FWD: Recusal Confirmation — Interview Panel Conflict Avoidance**
Timestamped two weeks ago.

*Jamie leans in, sees the date, and lets out a low, disbelieving laugh.*

jamiekerr: Two weeks.
jamiekerr: She tried to blow up something that was already handled.

*That’s the shift. Leonie hasn’t just interfered—she interfered after the ethical safeguard was already in place. Her mouth parts, but there’s nowhere graceful left to stand.*

leonieprice: I didn’t know it was formalized.

safiyadar: You didn’t ask. You acted.

*Your reply box is open now, white and waiting, attachment icon bright as a blade. Evidence in hand. Clock running toward morning.*

dialogue.speaker: System
dialogue.content: [MOMENTS LATER - NONE]

dialogue.speaker: User
dialogue.content: Make Leonie say, in front of everyone, why she went to HR instead of to you.

dialogue.speaker: The Group Chat
dialogue.content:
*The takeaway goes weirdly quiet around your table—fryer hiss, distant scooter outside, somebody at the counter laughing too loud and far away. Your screen throws cold light up your face. Leonie’s reflected in the black edge of it, all polish and no cover left.*

niahart: Say it properly, then. Why did you go to HR instead of me?

*Leonie folds her arms so tightly it looks painful. For one second she tries on dignity. Then she sees Safiya, Jamie, the forwarded timestamp on your screen, and something uglier, smaller, slips loose.*

leonieprice: Because if I came to you, you’d have had time to fix it.

*Jamie’s head snaps up.*

jamiekerr: Fix what?

*Leonie laughs once, brittle as snapped plastic.*

leonieprice: The story. The optics. All of it. You act like this is just friendship, but it’s always different for Nia, isn’t it? People make room. People bend rules. And she gets to still pretend she did it all clean.

*There it is. Not concern. Resentment with office vocabulary.*

Safiya’s stare turns flint-hard.

safiyadar: No. She applied clean. You wanted doubt to arrive first.

*Leonie doesn’t deny it. That silence is worse than a confession.*

The Group Chat: reveal landed. Her motive wasn’t ethics—it was pre-emptive sabotage dressed as fairness. Your draft email is still open, but now the next line writes itself.

dialogue.speaker: System
dialogue.content: [MOMENTS LATER - NONE]

dialogue.speaker: User
dialogue.content: Hand the phone to Jamie for thirty seconds while you write, before this turns into a shouting match.

dialogue.speaker: The Group Chat
dialogue.content:
*You shove the phone into Jamie’s palm before your own temper can get clever. The Notes app opens under your thumbs; white screen, blinking cursor, attachment icon waiting. Across the greasy tabletop, Jamie straightens like he’s been handed a live wire.*

jamiekerr: Right. Nobody talk over each other. Especially you.

*That last bit is aimed dead at Leonie. She bristles.*

jamiekerr: Priya? Hi. Quick one—Nia’s drafting the written statement now. You’ll have it tonight with Safiya’s recusal confirmation attached. Can you confirm the case stays logged as candidate interference once her email lands?

*Tiny pause. Keyboard in the background again.*

Priya on speaker: “Yes. Once Ms. Hart’s statement is received, I will close the matter under external interference and note that the prior report was unauthorized.”

*Jamie’s grin doesn’t reach his eyes.*

jamiekerr: Perfect. Cheers.

*He lowers the phone, then looks at Leonie with a flatness that wipes all the jokes off him.*

jamiekerr: There. It’s official. So if you say this was just concern one more time, you’re lying on record now.

*Leonie goes still. Not wounded—cornered.*

The Group Chat: shift made. The written statement isn’t just cleanup anymore; it’s the line that turns gossip into an accountable version of events.

dialogue.speaker: System
dialogue.content: [MOMENTS LATER - NONE]

dialogue.speaker: User
dialogue.content: Look up from the screen and tell Leonie she is not to discuss your candidacy again, anywhere.

dialogue.speaker: The Group Chat
dialogue.content:
*Your thumbs stop. Cursor blinking. Oil-salt air. Priya’s call ended, but the phone is still warm in Jamie’s hand when you lift your head and pin Leonie with the kind of steady that hurts more than volume.*

niahart: You do not discuss my candidacy again. Not at work, not in side chats, not as concern, not as gossip. Anywhere.

*It lands hard. No wobble in it. No room to wriggle.*

Leonie’s jaw shifts. For a second she looks like she might throw one last polished little knife. Then Safiya reaches over, taps your screen once, and quietly turns it toward the table.

At the top of the forwarded thread, just under the recusal confirmation, sits the original sender line Leonie clearly never expected anyone here to notice.

**From:** leonie.price@—
**CC:** Talent Inbox, Priya Menon, **M. Whelan**

*Jamie squints.*

jamiekerr: M. Whelan? That’s the other finalist.

*Silence. Then Leonie goes pale in a way foundation can’t fix.*

safiyadar: So this wasn’t just HR. You copied another candidate into an allegation.

*That changes everything. Not petty interference now—breach. Sloppy, panicked, provable breach.*

Your draft email glows below it, suddenly needing one more line.*
